raw_case_text: Twenty-six-year-old male patient referred from general hospital and admitted to our center with a history of Brucella aortic valve endocarditis, accompanied by hypotension and chest pain. Chest radiography showed moderately enlarged cardiac silhouette and mediastinum. Results of laboratory tests made on admission were as follow: White blood cell count, 19000/mm-3 with 91% neutrophils; platelet count, 89000/mm-3 ; hemoglobin, 8 g/dl; c-reactive protein, 54 mg/dl; erythrocyte sedimentation rate, 80 mm/h; blood urea nitrogen (BUN), 40 mg/dL; creatine (Cr), 2.9 mg/dL; and urinalysis revealed no any hematuria and 24-hour urinalysis (U.A) revealed proteinuria). Antinuclear antibody (ANA), antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA ), anti-double stranded DNA, rheumatic factor (RF), anticardiolopin antibody, lupus anticoagulant were all negative. Serum agglutination tests were positive (titer>1:1500), and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay tests for anti-Brucella IgG and IgM antibodies were strongly positive (133 U/ml and 31.7 U/ml; 30 U/ml and 20 U/ml, respectively). In addition, Brucella melitensis was isolated from 2 of 3 consecutive blood cultures. No significant alterations were observed in the electrocardiogram. TEE revealed normal aortic diameter at the mid-ascending aorta, severe aortic regurgitation, aortic ring abscess in noncoronary sinus, large vegetation in noncoronary sinus leaflet with preserved ventricular function and moderate pericardial effusion (Figure 1A and  1B). Aortic wall fistula from ring abscess to pericardium temporary was blocked by intra fistula vegetation. Intraoperative finding revealed large vegetation and perifistula hematoma in aortic wall. The fistula tract starting from aortic ring (Figures 2 and 3) and extended to aortic wall as intramural tract in a distance of 15 mm above the ring and ending to external aortic wall as a crater of fistula (Figure 4). We think that initial bleeding from fistula tract to pericardium was blocked by vegetation that confirmed intra operatively. The patient then underwent conventional surgical treatment with extracorporeal circulation (ECC), and replacement of aortic valve with prosthetic valve (carbomedic, sorin group, 23 mm size) and resection of aortic wall containing fistula site and its replacement with fresh pericardial patch (Figure 5). Patient treated with ceftriaxone 2 g and gentamicin 3 mg/kg prior to culture report. Therapy with doxycycline 100 mg twice daily with gentamicin 3 mg/kg intravenus in 2 divided doses with oral rifampin 600 mg once daily for 6 weeks was started after confirmation of Brucella endocarditis. The patient recovered uneventfully and was discharged in the 15th postoperative day.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 26-year-old male presented with chest pain and hypotension.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient was referred from a general hospital and admitted with hypotension, chest pain, and clinical features of acute aortic valve endocarditis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Prior medical history, comorbidities, and animal/dairy exposure not documented.
subjective.review_of_systems: Chest pain, hypotension. Home medications and allergies not documented.

objective.physical_examination: Hypotension; other vital signs and systemic physical examination details not documented beyond signs of acute endocarditis.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC: 19,000/mm^3 (91% neutrophils); Platelet count: 89,000/mm^3; Hemoglobin: 8 g/dL; CRP: 54 mg/dL; ESR: 80 mm/h; BUN: 40 mg/dL; Creatinine: 2.9 mg/dL. Urinalysis: no hematuria; 24-hour urine collection revealed proteinuria. Autoimmune/vasculitis panel: ANA, ANCA, anti-dsDNA, rheumatoid factor (RF), anticardiolipin antibody, and lupus anticoagulant were all negative. Chest radiography: moderately enlarged cardiac silhouette and widened mediastinum. ECG: no significant alterations.
objective.advanced_workup: Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE): normal mid-ascending aortic diameter, severe aortic regurgitation, aortic ring abscess in the noncoronary sinus, large mobile vegetation on the noncoronary cusp, preserved left ventricular function, moderate pericardial effusion, and an aortic wall fistula tract from the ring abscess extending 15 mm into the aortic wall and ending as a crater on the external aortic wall, temporarily plugged by intra-fistula vegetation. Surgical procedure: emergent open heart surgery under cardiopulmonary bypass with resection of the aortic wall containing the fistula tract, fresh autologous pericardial patch repair of the aortic wall defect, and aortic valve replacement with a 23 mm Carbomedics mechanical prosthesis. Intraoperative findings confirmed large vegetation and perifistula hematoma in the aortic wall.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Brucellar native aortic valve infective endocarditis complicated by aortic ring abscess, aorto-pericardial fistula, severe aortic regurgitation, and secondary acute glomerulonephritis/renal impairment.
Confirmation: Brucella melitensis isolated from 2 of 3 consecutive blood cultures; standard tube agglutination test positive at titer >1:1500; ELISA anti-Brucella IgG (133 U/mL; UNL 30) and IgM (31.7 U/mL; UNL 20) strongly positive.
Differentials ruled out: Autoimmune vasculitis and systemic lupus erythematosus ruled out (negative ANA, ANCA, anti-dsDNA, RF, anticardiolipin, and lupus anticoagulant).
Treatment & Outcome: Initially treated empirically with ceftriaxone 2 g and gentamicin 3 mg/kg. Upon confirmation, switched to oral doxycycline (100 mg BID), intravenous gentamicin (3 mg/kg/day in 2 divided doses), and oral rifampin (600 mg daily) for 6 weeks, alongside emergency surgical aortic valve replacement and pericardial patch repair. Recovered uneventfully and was discharged on postoperative day 15.
